title: Mulch Volume Calculator: Yards, Feet and Bags
description: Calculate mulch volume for any bed with the Mulch Volume Calculator — dimensions and depth into cubic yards, cubic feet and bag counts. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a 20 × 10 ft bed at 3 inches deep takes 50 cubic feet of mulch — 1.85 cubic yards, or 25 bags — the order written before the wheelbarrow ever moves.
quick_answer: The Mulch Volume Calculator works out how much mulch a bed needs from its dimensions and depth, reporting cubic yards for bulk delivery, cubic feet for pickup loads and the bag count for bagged product. Enter the bed's size and depth and read exactly what to buy.

20 × 10 ft at 3 in: 200 sq ft × 0.25 ft = 50 ft³ = 1.85 yd³. In bags: 25 of the 2 ft³ size, or 63 of the small 0.8 ft³ size — the small bags' convenience tax made visible.

Should I round the order up?
Yes — volumes round up to whole bags and sensible bulk fractions, and 10–20% extra covers settling and the bed that was bigger than remembered. Mulch keeps; delivery fees recur.
What about mulch against the house and trunks?
Keep mulch a few inches from siding and never volcano it against trunks — depth there is a pest and rot invitation. Those exclusions barely move the volume; they matter enormously to the trees.
Dyed, bark, straw, rubber — same volume math?
Identical geometry. Products differ in settling (straw compresses most, rubber least) and longevity, not in the cubic arithmetic of covering a bed.
